page: Amazon Web Services c8g.xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and custom AWS Graviton processors. It features an arm64 architecture utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 CPU model. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz, with no hyperthreading. Cache specifications include 64 KB of L1D cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the c8g.xlarge in the average tier for most operations. It achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1707.19 and a multi-core score of 6817.37. Memory bandwidth tests show 462.22 GB/sec for cached read-only operations and 96.22 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is a relative strength, scoring in the top 25% at 14.25 GB/sec, while multi-threaded decompression performs at an average rate of 55.73 GB/sec. However, the instance exhibits weaker performance in Passmark CPU tests, scoring 3836.85, and poor performance in Passmark CPU encryption at 750.07. Large language model inference speeds are also weak, generating 72.25 tokens per second on a small 135M model and 6.45 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the custom ARMv9 architecture offers a specialized hardware profile designed for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. The dedicated core allocation ensures consistent compute performance without resource contention. This instance is best suited for workloads such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 9.92 GB/sec, Redis database operations, and general-purpose single-threaded or multi-threaded tasks like software compilation and text processing.

The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Benchmark data indicates average performance across most compute and memory tests, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6817.37 and a static web serving throughput of 9.92 GB/sec. It demonstrates strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression but shows weaker results in Passmark CPU and encryption tests.
